levels.use: The page itself and what lies flat in it: the page background, bands, wells
Cards, panels and table frames in the flow of the page
Bars that stay while content scrolls under them: the page header, toolbars, sticky table headers, a settings bar
What opens over content without blocking it: menus, popovers, tooltips, toasts, date pickers, the navigation drawer
What blocks the page until it is answered or closed: dialogs, sheets, modal drawers — always with the scrim behind
An item while it is being dragged: it keeps its own surface, lifts above everything, and returns to its level when dropped

layers.name: layer.sticky
layers.use: Sticky bars and the page header: above the content that scrolls under them

layers.name: layer.floating
layers.use: Menus, popovers, tooltips and the navigation drawer: above sticky bars, so a menu opened from the header is never cut by it

layers.name: layer.modal
layers.use: Dialogs and their scrim: above everything the page shows, so nothing outside the dialog can be reached

layers.name: layer.toast
layers.use: Toasts and status messages: above dialogs, so a message is never hidden behind a scrim (it must not need an action while a dialog is open)

layers.name: layer.dragging
layers.use: An item being dragged: above everything while the pointer or keyboard holds it

shadowFormula: offsetY = max(1, ceil(height / 2)), blur = max(3, 2 × height), spread = −floor(height / 4); colour = the level's color.shadow step

edges.rule: The edge of whatever floats reaches 1.5:1 against every surface it can sit on (page, raised, sticky, another floating surface) and against the scrim, in Light and Dark

dark.rule: In Dark each rising level is lighter than the one below (≥ 1.1:1); floating and modal share the top surface and the scrim tells a modal apart

topLayer.what: The browser's top layer sits above every z-index: a <dialog> opened with showModal() and an element with the popover attribute go there, in the order they opened. Layer numbers order everything else.
topLayer.dialog: <dialog class="ds-modal" aria-labelledby="…"> … </dialog> opened with dialog.showModal(); its ::backdrop is the scrim; Escape closes it; return focus to the opener
topLayer.popover:
…
with
topLayer.toast:
…
, shown after any open dialog

must: open with showModal() (or role="dialog" + aria-modal="true" + .ds-scrim when <dialog> can't be used)
a label: aria-labelledby pointing at the dialog's heading
focus moves into the dialog when it opens (the first field, or the dialog itself)
focus stays inside while it is open; the page behind is inert
Escape closes it (unless closing would lose work: then it asks)
focus returns to the control that opened it

forcedColors.what: Forced colours (Windows contrast themes) remove every box-shadow and replace surfaces with the system page colour: every level looks flat. Borders stay, drawn in the system text colour.
tokensCss: .ds-floating, .ds-modal and .ds-dragging draw a border on every side, .ds-sticky on the side facing the content
the drawer pane of .ds-shell draws its edge
you: never remove the border of a floating level (ER-04)
show hover and press with something besides the shadow (ER-08)
keep focus rings on: a shadow is never a focus indicator

classes.use: Cards, panels, table frames in the flow of the page: raised surface and shadow
A bar that stays while content scrolls under it: sticky at the top, sticky layer, surface, shadow and a line on its bottom edge (data-stick="end": at the bottom, line on top)
classes.tailwind: sticky top-0 z-(--ds-layer-sticky) bg-elevation-sticky-surface shadow-sticky border-b-line border-elevation-sticky-border

classes.use: Menus, popovers, tooltips, toasts, the navigation drawer: floating layer, surface, shadow and an edge on every side (data-layer="toast": the toast layer)
Dialogs and sheets: modal layer, surface, shadow, edge; its ::backdrop is the scrim
classes.tailwind: z-(--ds-layer-modal) bg-elevation-modal-surface shadow-modal border-line border-elevation-modal-border backdrop:bg-elevation-modal-scrim

classes.use: The scrim for a modal that is not a <dialog>: fixed over the page, just before the dialog in the same layer
An item while it is dragged: the dragging layer, shadow and edge; it keeps its own surface

checks.title: Whatever floats keeps an edge — never shadow alone (forced colours remove shadows) — and a modal has its scrim
Height shows by surface where shadows can't: in Dark each level is lighter than the one below (≥ 1.1:1); in Light no level is darker than the page
Edges are seen: the edge of whatever floats reaches 1.5:1 against every surface it can sit on and against the scrim, in Light and Dark
Shadows grow with height: a higher level drops further, blurs wider and is at least as dark, in Light and Dark
Text reads on every level: each surface is measured with every text colour (C1), in Light and Dark
The stacking order holds: sticky < floating < modal < toast < dragging, product layers in between, and tokens.css stacks only with layer tokens

rules.rule: Shadows come from a level: box-shadow is var(--ds-elevation-<job>-shadow) or none (Tailwind shadow-raised, shadow-sticky, shadow-floating, shadow-modal, shadow-dragging). No shadow written by hand, none of Tailwind's own (shadow-sm … shadow-2xl, drop-shadow-*), no filter: drop-shadow() on a surface.
rules.why: A hand-made shadow belongs to no level: it doesn't grow with height, doesn't switch for Dark, and nobody can tell what sits on what.

rules.rule: Never use the shadow colours or alpha primitives in a shadow (--ds-color-shadow-*, --ds-color-black-alpha-*). Pick the level.
rules.why: They are the strengths the levels pick from; a shadow made from them by hand skips the order the build checks.

rules.rule: A level's surface and shadow go together: the shadow of floating goes on the floating surface, never on a card's. Use the class (.ds-raised … .ds-dragging) to take the whole level.
rules.why: In Dark the surface is what shows height; a floating shadow on a raised surface sits at one height and looks like another.

rules.rule: Whatever floats has its edge: floating, modal and dragging draw border: var(--ds-border-width-line) solid var(--ds-elevation-<job>-border) on every side; a sticky bar draws its line on the side facing the content.
rules.why: Forced colours remove every shadow, and in Dark a shadow barely shows: without a border a menu has no edge and its items run into the page.

rules.rule: Stacking uses layers: z-index is var(--ds-layer-<job>) (Tailwind z-(--ds-layer-floating)). Raw numbers only -1, 0, 1 and 2, for order inside one component. Never 999 or 9999.
rules.why: Stray numbers race each other: a dropdown at 9999 paints over an open dialog and its scrim, and a sticky header at 1000 covers the menu opened from it.

rules.rule: A modal is modal: a <dialog> opened with showModal() (not the open attribute), its ::backdrop the scrim (var(--ds-elevation-modal-scrim)). A dialog built without <dialog> has role="dialog", aria-modal="true", a .ds-scrim behind it, focus moved in and held, the page behind made inert, Escape to close, and focus returned on close.
rules.why: Without it, keyboard and screen-reader users walk out of the dialog into a page they can't see past the scrim.

rules.rule: Height in Dark comes from the tokens: never override shadows or level surfaces for dark mode ([data-theme="dark"] or prefers-color-scheme rules that set box-shadow or an elevation background).
rules.why: The tokens already switch: Dark lifts surfaces (lighter as they rise) because a darker shadow on a near-black page measures almost nothing.

rules.rule: Hover and press never lift alone: a :hover or :active rule that changes box-shadow also changes the fill (color.bg.surface-hover), a border colour or an outline. Press goes back down, never up.
rules.why: A shadow change is removed in forced colours and barely shows in Dark: for many people nothing happens under the pointer.

rules.rule: No glass: floating and modal surfaces are opaque — no backdrop-filter, no translucent background, no opacity on the surface.
rules.why: Text contrast on a see-through surface depends on whatever scrolls behind it, so it can't be measured — and it fails exactly when the page behind is busy.

rules.rule: Never redefine elevation or layer variables in app code (--ds-elevation-*, --ds-layer-*). Add a product layer in the engine config (elevation.layers) and build.
rules.why: An overridden level skips the checks that keep edges visible, surfaces rising in Dark and layers in order.

decisions.what: Does it need height at all
decisions.question: What should set it apart?
answers: Things that belong together, with room around them
space (Spacing: a bigger stack or inline gap) — no level
A region of the page (a sidebar, a band, a well)
a surface change (color.bg.surface-sunken) or a border.width.line edge — no shadow
Many cards side by side (a dashboard, a grid of results)
elevation.raised, or only a border.width.line outline: a page of shadows is noise
Something that sits over other content
a level from the next table — the higher it sits, the more it interrupts

decisions.question: Where does it sit, and what does it do to the page?
answers: It is the page, or lies flat in it
elevation.page — the page surface, no shadow
It groups content in the flow of the page (a card, a panel, a table frame)
elevation.raised (.ds-raised)
It stays while content scrolls under it (the page header, a toolbar, a sticky table header)
elevation.sticky (.ds-sticky; data-stick="end" for a bar along the bottom)
It opens over content and the page stays usable (a menu, popover, tooltip, toast, date picker, the navigation drawer)
elevation.floating (.ds-floating), opened as a popover so it sits in the top layer
It must be answered or closed before the page can be used (a dialog, a sheet, a modal drawer)
elevation.modal (.ds-modal) on a <dialog> opened with showModal(): the scrim, the edge and the layer come with it
It is being dragged
elevation.dragging (.ds-dragging) while it is held; back to its own level when dropped

decisions.question: What has to be on top?
answers: A menu opened from the sticky header
nothing to do: layer.floating is above layer.sticky
A menu, select or tooltip inside a dialog
open it as a popover (top layer: it goes above the dialog) — or keep it inside the dialog's own box; never a bigger z-index
A menu inside a card or table that clips (overflow: hidden or auto)
a popover: the top layer is never clipped by a parent; a z-index can't escape overflow
A toast while a dialog is open
layer.toast (.ds-floating data-layer="toast"), opened as popover="manual" after the dialog; it must not need an action, because the page outside the dialog is inert
Something the system doesn't have a place for (a banner over sticky bars, a help panel)
a product layer in the config (elevation.layers, "above": the layer below it) — the number is computed

decisions.question: Does it change while someone uses it?
answers: Hover on something clickable (a card that is a link)
color.bg.surface-hover or a border colour — a bigger shadow may come with it, never alone
Press
back to its resting level (never higher): it moves toward the page
Keyboard focus
the focus ring (tokens.css draws it) — never a shadow
Drag
elevation.dragging while held, plus a keyboard way to move it (buttons or arrow keys); back to its level on drop

mistakes.mistake: A menu set apart from the page by its shadow alone
mistakes.measured: its shadow reaches 1.23:1 against the page in Light and 1.05:1 in Dark; forced colours remove it altogether — the menu's items run into the page
mistakes.fixValue: the edge `elevation.floating.border`: at least 1.68:1 (Light) and 1.58:1 (Dark) against anything a menu can sit on, measured beside its own shadow, and kept in forced colours

mistakes.measured: even at 56% black, the modal shadow reaches 1.06:1 on the Dark page — there is almost nothing left to darken
mistakes.fixValue: in Dark the floating surface is 1.58:1 lighter than the page; the tokens switch by themselves

mistakes.measured: it is above `layer.modal` (300) and `layer.dragging` (500): left open, it paints over a dialog and its scrim
mistakes.fixValue: 200: above sticky bars (100), below dialogs (300); a popover sits in the top layer and is never clipped

mistakes.mistake: A dialog on the card surface (color.bg.surface) in Dark
mistakes.measured: against the scrim over the page it reaches 1.29:1, and it looks like one more card
mistakes.fixValue: 1.75:1 for the modal surface, plus its edge (2.77:1)

mistakes.mistake: A card that shows hover only by a bigger shadow
mistakes.measured: in Dark the raised and sticky shadows reach 1.04:1 and 1.05:1 (1/3px against 2/6px) — the change is close to invisible, and gone in forced colours
mistakes.fixValue: 1.36:1 against the card in Light; the shadow may change too, never alone

mistakes.mistake: A frosted-glass menu (backdrop-filter: blur, translucent background)
mistakes.measured: its text contrast depends on whatever scrolls behind it, so no build can measure it — it fails exactly when the page behind is busy
mistakes.fixValue: opaque: every text colour measured on it (E5)

mistakes.mistake: A <dialog> shown with the open attribute
mistakes.measured: it opens without the top layer, the backdrop or an inert page: Tab walks out of the dialog into the page behind it
mistakes.fixValue: top layer, ::backdrop scrim, page inert, Escape closes; return focus to the button that opened it
